title: Residual Connections & Layer Normalization — Normalize Before or After the Block
key_insight: Post-norm applies a block then normalizes the sum. Pre-norm normalizes before the block and adds the result back to the untouched residual stream.
body:
## Normalize Before or After the Block

The same attention and feed-forward parts train differently depending on where normalization sits relative to the residual addition.

Post-norm applies a block then normalizes the sum. Pre-norm normalizes before the block and adds the result back to the untouched residual stream.

Pre-norm often makes very deep training easier because gradients have a cleaner residual route, though architecture details still matter.
common_mistakes: Residual connections permanently skip every transformation.
Layer normalization averages unrelated users together.
Normalization removes all learned scale and shift.
mini_exercise: Draw “Normalize Before or After the Block” as three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: These support stable information and gradient flow through deep transformer stacks.
